body.statement: For the worked binary input, the deterministic run performs ancestor restriction to \(Y^{*}=\{Y\}\), computes \(D^{*}=\{Y\}\) and a closure containing \(S,A\), enters Algorithm 2, exhausts every line-7 candidate, and records \(\operatorname{LGSFailA2NoCandidate}(D^{*},C)\).  Its fixed residual generator deterministically produces, and its verifier accepts, the rational-affine contrast \(d=(-4,-1,0,3)\) on \(0<b<1/32\).  At \(b=1/64\) the two canonical models have selector support exactly \(H=\{0,1\}\), the same complete observed law including \(W_0,Z_0\), strictly positive admissible cells, and target probabilities \(1/2\) and \(63/128\).
body.proof_tex:
We first reduce the graphical cases for the displayed binary input.  In the target LS-SWIG, \(A\) and \(S\) are fixed, while \(W_0\) and \(Z_0\) have no children.  Therefore the random ancestor set of \(Y\) and its only district are
\[
 Y^*=\{Y\},\qquad D^*=\{Y\}.
\tag{1}
\]
In the observed latent projection, the shared root \(U_0\) induces \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), the shared root \(R_0\) induces \(S\leftrightarrow Y\), and the directed edges are \(S\to A\) and \(A\to Y\).  The isolated vertices \(W_0,Z_0\) are fixable.  Neither \(S\) nor \(A\) is fixable while \(S,A,Y\) remain: in each case its district intersects its descendants in more than the vertex itself.  Hence no reachable superset of \(D^*\) can omit \(S\) or \(A\), whereas \(\{S,A,Y\}\) is reachable by fixing \(W_0,Z_0\).  By \(\textnormal{lem:computed-closure-valid-sequence}\), the computed closure is
\[
 C=\{S,A,Y\}\supsetneq D^*.
\tag{2}
\]
Because \(S\in C\), the deterministic case function enters Algorithm 2.

Here \(\operatorname{ch}^*(S)=\{A\}\).  At \(s=0\), \(A\) is laid back and the serious set is empty, so this context supplies no admissible nonempty-serious triple.  At \(\bar s=1\), the known selector gate forces \(A=1\), giving the only possible pair \(Z=\{A\}\), \(z=1\).  The districts of the mechanically constructed LS-SWIG partition their vertex set, so at most one district \(D'\) contains \(D^*\), and the machine computes that district rather than receiving it as data.  For the resulting candidate, the bidirected edge induced by \(R_0\) leaves \(S\) adjacent to \(Y(\bar s)\).  The line-7 conditioning set does not block this length-one path, so the required d-separation fails.  There is no other supported nonempty-serious triple.  Canonical enumeration therefore exhausts and records
\[
 \operatorname{LGSFailA2NoCandidate}(D^*,C),
\tag{3}
\]
then creates the corresponding residual task.  Equations (1)--(3) use only the input graph and current state, as required by \(\textnormal{prop:input-determinacy}\).

We next verify the residual contrast.  Index the four \(A=1\) natural response rows by \((u_0,r_0)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), and set
\[
 r=(3/4,1/4,1/4,3/4),
 \qquad d=(-4,-1,0,3).
\tag{4}
\]
After positive common denominators are cleared, the two observation rows affected by these response probabilities form the rational matrix
\[
 M=\begin{pmatrix}2&1&6&3\\1&2&1&2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{rref}(M)=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0&11/3&4/3\\0&1&-4/3&1/3\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{5}
\]
The fixed free-column enumeration sets the third free coordinate to zero and the fourth to three, producing \(d\); direct multiplication gives
\[
 Md^{\mathsf T}=0.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus the fixed generator obtains \(d\) by rational row reduction of the residual observation map, rather than receiving a desired contrast.

For a binary response subtable \(f\in\{0,1\}^4\), define
\[
 \pi_0(f)=\prod_{j=1}^4r_j^{f(j)}(1-r_j)^{1-f(j)},
\tag{7}
\]
\[
 \delta(f)=\pi_0(f)\sum_{j=1}^4
 \frac{d_j\{f(j)-r_j\}}{r_j(1-r_j)},
 \qquad
 \pi_b(f)=\pi_0(f)+b\delta(f).
\tag{8}
\]
Keep the \(A=0\) response rows at their baseline law and combine them with (8), thereby obtaining a law on the full finite canonical response tables.  Independence of the four Bernoulli coordinates under \(\pi_0\) gives
\[
 \sum_f\delta(f)=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_f\pi_b(f)f(j)=r_j+bd_j
 \quad(j=1,\ldots,4).
\tag{9}
\]
For each \(f\), the score multiplying \(b\) in (8) is bounded below by
\[
 -\frac{16}{3}-4-12=-\frac{64}{3}.
\tag{10}
\]
Consequently, if \(0<b<1/32\), then
\[
 \pi_b(f)\geq \pi_0(f)\left(1-\frac{64b}{3}\right)
 >\frac13\pi_0(f)>0.
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (9)--(11) prove normalization and strict simplex membership on the rational open box, consistently with canonical-response richness.

The selector and natural-treatment equations give
\[
 \Pr(S=0\mid R_0=0)=\frac23,
 \qquad
 \Pr(S=0\mid R_0=1)=\frac13,
\tag{12}
\]
with the probabilities reversed for \(S=1\), and
\[
 \Pr(A=1\mid U_0=0,S=0)=\frac14,
 \qquad
 \Pr(A=1\mid U_0=1,S=0)=\frac34.
\tag{13}
\]
Since \((U_0,R_0)\) is uniform, the coefficient of \(b\) in the natural-context cell \(\Pr(S=0,A=1,Y=1)\) is
\[
 \frac14\frac23\left\{\frac14(-4)+\frac34(0)\right\}
 +\frac14\frac13\left\{\frac14(-1)+\frac34(3)\right\}=0.
\tag{14}
\]
In the forced context \(S=1,A=1\), that coefficient is
\[
 \frac14\frac13(-4+0)+\frac14\frac23(-1+3)=0.
\tag{15}
\]
No \(A=0\) response row is perturbed.  Equality of each corresponding \(Y=0\) cell follows from its unchanged \((S,A)\) margin and (14)--(15).  Direct finite summation over \(u_0,r_0\in\{0,1\}\), using (12)--(13) and the baseline response probabilities (4), gives in the stipulated order
\[
 \bigl\{p(S,A,Y)\bigr\}
 =(13,11,13,11,24,24)/96.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (14)--(15) make (16) constant throughout the box.  Its smallest entry is \(11/96>0\).  Appending independent fair \(W_0,Z_0\) multiplies every full observed cell by \(1/4\), so the two complete observed laws agree and every admissible cell remains positive.  Equation (12) and the fair law of \(R_0\) give
\[
 \Pr(S=0)=\Pr(S=1)=\frac12,
\tag{17}
\]
so selector support is exactly \(H=\{0,1\}\).

Under \(do(A=1,S=s_{\emptyset})\), the independent pair \((U_0,R_0)\) remains uniform.  From (4) and (9),
\[
 T_b(Y=1)=\frac12+b\frac{-4-1+0+3}{4}
 =\frac12-\frac b2.
\tag{18}
\]
The simplex inequalities (11), observation identities (14)--(16), exact support (17), strict admissible-cell positivity, and the constant nonzero sign in (18) are precisely the residual verifier's acceptance tests.  It therefore accepts the rational-affine pair consisting of the baseline model at \(b=0\) and the perturbed model at \(b\), for every \(0<b<1/32\).  At \(b=1/64\), their targets are respectively
\[
 \frac12
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \frac12-\frac1{128}=\frac{63}{128},
\tag{19}
\]
while (16) and the independent nuisance factors show equality of the complete observed law.  This proves every asserted component of the worked certificate.
body.justification: The example follows the deterministic path through Algorithm 2 to its unclassified line-9 failure and only then obtains nonidentification from an independently generated and verified affine response contrast.
body.gap: The corrected execution removes the former hand-installed trace and proves the null contrast, simplex interior, observed-law equality, exact selector support, and target separation directly.
body.consumer: The exact cells, affine canonical table path, failure tag, and target contrast form a regression fixture for the redesigned backend.
